Jordan Lee: Hey folks, quick onboarding question. I have a live-coding session + short recording tomorrow from my office laptop that will call the hosted API. Is it OK to use our project hosted key for this, or should I request a demo/ephemeral key?

Marta Silva: welcome Jordan! Use an ephemeral key if possible (Console -> API Keys -> Ephemeral). If you must use the hosted key, keep it in the company vault and never commit. Also be mindful of quota: per-key concurrent streams and per-project tokens/minute are the usual limits.

Jordan Lee: i hit a 429 earlier and saw Retry-After: 5. Any tiny curl loop that honors Retry-After i can drop into my demo script?

Marta Silva: small bash pattern: 
```bash
# simple retry honoring Retry-After header
for i in 1 2 3; do
  resp=$(curl -s -D - -o /tmp/body -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json)
  ra=$(grep -i "Retry-After" /tmp/body | awk '{print $2}' | tr -d '\r')
  status=$(echo "$resp" | head -n1)
  if [[ "$status" != *"429"* ]]; then cat /tmp/body; break; fi
  sleep ${ra:-$((2**i))}
done
```

ops-bot: To request a temporary quota bump or IP allowlist for demos, open https://redwood.internal/support/new with subject "Demo quota bump" and include email, team, demo window, and expected concurrent sessions. Ops usually replies within a few hours.

sec-bot: If you accidentally post a key anywhere public, rotate it immediately and file a security incident at https://redwood.internal/security/incident. We'll help audit usage.

Jordan Lee: thanks all 64f I'll create an ephemeral key for the recording and open a ticket if i need an allowlist. Appreciate the help!
